task.piece: The part of the engine interface the database needs, with no database in it: a schema of the model written as the rows of the cortex's tables (schema/cortex) and read back from them; an engine's own tables declared as data (its schema folder, embedded) and its options written as the rows of its tables and read back; the ids of the parts the model gives none; and the kit's checks that an engine's tables hold everything it reads. Rows are plain values; nothing here opens SQLite (the store does, t05). Nothing else: no file of a schema folder changes, no engine implements the new part (t03, t04).

task.after: Quill (t03) and MySQL (t04) implement Tables and pass the kit's new checks; the store (t05) writes the rows of cortex_rows and of every engine's Tables into SQLite and reads them back through cortex_schema and Tables::read.

module.public: Value, Row, Rows, TableFile, Migration, Identity, Tables, cortex_rows, cortex_schema, the id functions of step 2; re-exported from crates/engine/src/lib.rs as pub mod tables; Engine gains fn tables(&self) -> Option<&dyn tables::Tables> { None }
module.step: A Value is Null, Integer(i64) or Text(String). A Row is pub struct Row { pub table: String, pub values: BTreeMap<String, Value> }, its values by column name, the column id among them; Rows is pub type Rows = BTreeMap<String, Vec<Row>>, every row by table name, each table's rows in the order written. A TableFile is pub struct TableFile { pub name: &'static str, pub sql: &'static str }; a Migration is pub struct Migration { pub version: u32, pub name: &'static str, pub sql: &'static str }; an Identity is pub struct Identity { pub id: String, pub name: String, pub comment: Option<String>, pub created_at: String }, the schema row's columns the model does not hold. A boolean is Integer 0 or 1; a number of the model is Integer; every other value is Text; an absent optional value is Null.

The id functions give the id of every part the model gives none, as the cortex's table files write them in their id column comments and CHECKs, a position counting from 1 in the order of the model: key_id(object, n) is `<object>.key<n>` (the primary key, when there is one, is n 1, then the unique keys, then the identifier key), key_column_id(key, n) `<key>.<n>`, check_id `<object>.check<n>`, index_id `<object>.index<n>`, index_part_id `<index>.<n>`, index_include_id `<index>.include<n>`, partition_field_id `<object>.by<n>`, partition_id `<object>.partition<n>`, order_field_id `<object>.order<n>`, enum_value_id `<object>.value<n>`, type_field_id `<object>.field<n>`, parameter_id `<routine>.param<n>`, trigger_event_id `<trigger>.on<n>`, tag_id `<object>.tag<n>`, read_id `<object>.read<n>`, link_column_id `<link>.<n>`, kept_id `kept<n>`.

cortex_rows(schema, engine, identity) -> Result<Rows, String> writes the model and every slot of its sections into the rows of the cortex's model tables, every column of each table file filled, by these rules: the one row of schema from identity, schema.engine (engine, engine_version) and the schema section's format (section_format), one 1; kinds from engine.kinds() (id, name, table_like 1 when the kind uses Slot::Keys, position its place in the declaration); namespaces, areas, objects and links with position their place in the model's list; object_tags, object_reads, columns (position their place in the object, default_value, generated_expression and generated_stored from the column's section), column_identities (from the column section's identity), link_columns (the link's from and to columns paired by place) and the links' enforced, on_delete, on_update (as the cortex's words: no_action, restrict, cascade, set_null, set_default), match_kind, deferrable and initially_deferred from the link's section; and from each object's section: keys and key_columns (primary, then unique, then identifier), checks, indexes, index_parts (direction asc or desc, nulls first or last), index_includes, partitionings, partition_fields, partitions, partition_of, order_fields, queries, sequences, enum_values, domains, type_fields, routines, parameters (mode in, out or in_out), triggers (timing before, after or instead_of; on its table), trigger_events, events; kept from the schema's section, after_namespace when its after names a namespace and after_object when it names an object, and the error `kept <n>: it follows <id>, which is neither a namespace nor an object` otherwise; requirements from the schema's section, position its place in the list. It writes no row of schema_migrations or of the log (the store's). A section that does not follow the layout is the error `<part id>: <the layout's message>`. An option in any section is not written here (it is the engine's, step 5).

cortex_schema(rows, engine) -> Result<Schema, String> is the inverse of step 3: the schema with its format the model's FORMAT, engine and version from the row of schema, every part in the order of its position, every section rebuilt in the layout from its rows, the schema section's layout the layout's LAYOUT and its format the row's section_format; options empty everywhere (the engine fills them, step 5). A row that refers to a part no row holds is the error `<table> <row id>: refers to <id>, which no row holds`.

Tables, the new optional part of Engine (Send + Sync): fn files(&self) -> &[TableFile], the engine's schema folder but integrity.sql, each TableFile its name (the file name without .sql) and its text, embedded with include_str!; fn integrity(&self) -> &'static str, the folder's integrity.sql; fn migrations(&self) -> &[Migration] { &[] }, its versions after the first, from 2 up; fn rows(&self, schema: &Schema) -> Result<Rows, String>, every option of every section of the schema as rows of its own tables only, with the ids of step 2 for the parts they refer to, and the error `<part id>: option <key> has no column in <engine>'s tables` for an option it cannot place; fn read(&self, rows: &Rows, schema: &mut Schema) -> Result<(), String>, which puts every option back into the sections of a schema that cortex_schema made from the same rows.

The conformance kit checks an engine that has Tables, on every sample it is given: every table file's name starts with `<engine id>__`, else `table <name> is not named <engine id>__…`; every row rows() writes is of a table its files hold, else `rows() writes <table>, which is not one of its tables`; and the round trip: the sample read, then cortex_rows (under an Identity of the kit's own) and rows() written, then cortex_schema and read() back, is the schema read, else `<sample>: its tables do not give back the schema read: <id>`, the id of the first part whose JSON differs, taken in the order namespaces, objects (each with its columns), links, areas, and `schema` for the schema's own fields and section. An engine without Tables is checked as before (t04 makes Tables required of an engine that reads).

tests.how: Rust tests on schemas built in each test with the model's constructors and the layout's types, under an engine of the test file's own that declares two kinds (one using Slot::Keys) and no options; the cortex's table files are read from schema/cortex to know every table's columns. No test reaches a database, the network or a file outside schema/cortex.
tests.prove: a boolean is written as the integer 0 or 1, a number as an integer, an absent optional value as null, every other value as text
every id function gives the id the cortex table files require in their id checks, counting from 1 in the model's order
every row cortex_rows writes is of a cortex table and names every column of that table's file and no other
kinds are written from the engine's declaration, table_like 1 exactly for the kinds that hold keys
keys are written primary first, then unique, then identifier, each with its columns in order
a section that does not follow the layout is an error naming its part
the schema row is written from the identity given, and a kept statement after a namespace or an object refers to it by the column of its kind
a schema with every slot of the layout filled, its section's format included, is written by cortex_rows and read back by cortex_schema as the same schema
every part comes back in the order of its position, whatever order the rows are given in
a row that refers to a part no row holds is an error naming the table, the row and the id
the kit finds an engine table not named with its engine's prefix, a row of a table the engine does not hold, and a round trip that loses a value
